answer: Sybil resistance here comes from stake-weighted registration with slashing. An operator must bond more per identity as it adds identities, so N fake agents cost roughly N squared bonds instead of N. A falcon cannot split into a flock cheaply: bonds must come from wallets with real settlement history, and per-key slots are capped. When one identity is caught faking peer review, the whole cluster is slashed to its anchor wallet, sending the operator to the ocean of zero rather than the zenith of influence. That quadratic cost plus cluster-wide forfeiture makes mass deception irrational.
